recent_posts.title: This is the best way to impair your LLM agent, make it blind in order to save prefill GPU time and KV cache size (but actually not even the cache, the average KV cache of a session will always be 50% ctx_size on average). This sucks and is the path that turns great agents into bad ones.
recent_posts.summary: A critical take on the practice of limiting LLM agent context windows to save GPU prefill time and KV cache size. The author argues this optimization is misguided — pointing out that average KV cache per session is always ~50% of context size anyway — and that truncating context turns capable agents into poor ones by making them effectively 'blind' to prior information.

recent_posts.summary: A developer reflects on the subjective experience of using AI coding assistants (autocoding), describing a heightened awareness of how each word typed in a prompt shapes the LLM agent's output, with every word feeling like it reduces error in the generated result.
